newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures rise after tame PPI figures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures rise after tame PPI figures.

text.p: U.S. debt futures rose to moderate gains after wholesale-level inflation figures for last month proved more benign than expected.
The producer price index fell 0.6 percent and the core rate dipped 0.1 percent. Economists had expected PPI to stay flat, with a 0.1-percent rise in the core inflation rate.
March business inventories rose 0.3 percent, as forecast.

June U.S. Treasury bond futures, which had straddled unchanged at the open, shot up half a point in busy trade and returned above 100- and 200-day moving averages at 109-31/32 and 110-03/32, respectively, before giving back some gains.
Brokers said the contract met sizable offers on the rise, with some noting rumors that a large hedge fund was selling.

They also said nervousness persisted about the possibility that the Federal Reserve will move May 20 to tighten credit policy again in another preemptive move against inflation, which the Fed has warned could flare especially if the nation's labor markets remain tight.
"The market is worried about next week," explained one T-bond futures floor broker of why June T-bonds curtailed the rise sparked by the biggest one-month drop in producer prices since August 1993.
The rise barely tugged nearby T-bonds above Monday's settlement at 110-12/32 before buying abated.

Floor brokers appeared impressed, however, by June T-bond's ability to hold intraday supports near 110-04/32 and 109-28/32 after the opening probe to the minus side lacked power to punch below Tuesday's low at 109-24/32 and more support pegged at 109-22/32.
"At 30 (110-30/32) could be our objective," added the broker of the intraday outlook.
"I think we're going to take it higher and will retest 13 (110-13/32), maybe 20 (110-20/32)," said a another broker.
In the short end, December Eurodollars also met good selling on the rise, which petered out as players also eyed the May 20 open market committee meeting with trepidation.
"There're good flows, but the market's got a little bit of a cap on it," said one Eurodollar floor broker. "I think we're going to settle in here."

He said many of his customers are positioning themselves in anticipation of a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike next week but that he thought Eurodollar futures might have more upside because they are priced too cheap to cash if the Fed does nothing and leaves rates unchanged.

At 0824 CDT/1324 GMT, June T-bonds rose 13/32 to 110-07/32, 10-year notes rose 8/32 to 107-13/32, muni-bonds gained 13/32 to 116-00, June T-bills rose 0.015 bp to 94.740, and December Eurodollars gained 0.040 bp to 93.71.
